text: With the raw JSON parsing proven, this lesson puts real change tracking in place: a Stream, watching the raw table for anything new, with no watermark column for anyone to manage by hand.

That's the entire statement. CREATE STREAM, ON TABLE, pointed at the raw table. From this moment forward, the Stream tracks every row inserted, updated, or deleted — starting now, not retroactively pulling in the table's full history.

A Stream doesn't store a copy of the changed rows. It stores an offset, a marker for where it last left off, and computes what's changed since then on demand. That offset only moves forward when a DML statement that successfully commits references the Stream — a plain SELECT on its own doesn't advance anything, which makes it completely safe to re-run while you're exploring.

Every row a Stream returns carries three extra metadata columns. METADATA dollar ACTION reports INSERT or DELETE. METADATA dollar ISUPDATE flags whether a row is one half of an update. METADATA dollar ROW underscore ID pairs an update's two halves together. And this function, SYSTEM dollar STREAM underscore HAS underscore DATA, is exactly what next lesson's Task checks before doing any work at all.
With the Stream in place and proven safe to query, next lesson writes the one thing that actually changes data: a Task, gated on that same HAS_DATA check, running a real MERGE.
